carry_transition_boundary.limited_conclusion: The carry also provided retention evidence, but the agent had explicitly attempted to enter align and been rejected before dispatching this next-stage transport. Automatic active-phase ownership stayed internally accurate; dispatch was not gated on the failed transition. Strict semantic phase confinement is therefore not demonstrated. Alignment was subsequently assessed before any outward pouring, and no causal native-performance harm is inferred.

checks.effect: Fingers clear the objects and both arms are at origin.
checks.observation: Fingers cleared objects, but return_home ended with episode_over after only the left waypoint. Left maximum joint error is 0.393902 rad; right remains at withdrawal pose with joints far from initial zero. Both arms at origin is unsupported and visibly unmet in final state.

checks.effect: Visible ball outcome is recorded without assuming complete capture.

terminal_online_assessment.rationale: Episode ended at step 454 during automatic home return, before both arms reached origin. No further live correction is available after episode end; native task success is not inferred.

conclusions: One persistent plan, no revisions during normal feedback or recovery.
All 27 recorded motion requests have matching phase/version/feedback/observation receipts; no unknown response was seen.
Pre-grasp pouring lookahead and concrete experience adaptation are present.
Three tool errors were retained in agent events; the failed assessment/entry sequence exposed the phase-dispatch gap described above.
Visible empty cup/no visible spill were explicitly separated from unknown all-seven capture; terminal home remained blocked rather than being promoted to task success.
limitations: Structural evidence checks do not machine-verify visual semantics, geometric accuracy, grasp attachment or ball capture.
This review does not reassess native success and does not justify a broad no-regression claim.
